title: When the Harbor Breaks
premise: In 1946, Mirabel Halloran works as a census taker in a war-scarred harbor town, using the position to quietly document the soldiers and deserters the official record erases—names he kept as a battlefield nurse and swore never to surrender. When his ledger is discovered by Odile Ferrant, a widow running a boatyard that shelters the very people he's cataloguing, the two form an uneasy alliance: she offers refuge, he offers testimony, and together they race to complete the record before a government auditor razes the yard and everyone hidden inside it. The workshop burns in the final act, but Mirabel chooses exposure over silence, reading the names aloud at the inquiry, and the found family scatters yet survives—each name finally written into the official history he once kept in secret.
about_author: August Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade restoring damaged municipal records from coastal towns. Their fiction is drawn from the marginalia—pencil notes, unstamped pages, and names that official histories forgot to carry forward.

chapters.title: The Question That Wasn't on the Form
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On a routine census round, a dockworker's widow asks Mirabel whether the dead count too, and he answers too honestly, revealing he keeps his own ledger. The beat is a hairline crack: fifteen years of practiced invisibility fissure in a single unguarded sentence.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Unlisted
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashback. We see the battlefield origins of his book of names—officers who reported fewer dead than fell—and his arrival in the harbor town. The beat is the weight of witness: he realizes the ledger is a promise he cannot keep and cannot break.

chapters.title: The Boatyard That Keeps Its Own Records
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile Ferrant notices the census taker lingering at her gate and confronts him, discovering his ledger contains her late husband's name, misreported as a deserter. The beat is hostile recognition turning to wary alliance: two keepers of suppressed truths.

chapters.title: Names in the Hull
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Odile reveals the boatyard shelters deserters and displaced families; Mirabel offers to enter them in his ledger as living testimony. The beat is tentative trust—found family assembling around a shared act of record-keeping.

chapters.title: The Auditor Arrives
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Government auditor Corvane arrives to assess the yard for demolition, and Mirabel recognizes him as an officer whose falsified reports he once copied. The beat is dread: the man who taught him which silences keep people safe now holds the power to erase them all.

chapters.title: What Odile Won't Burn
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Corvane offers Odile a clean demolition in exchange for surrendering the yard's irregular residents. She refuses, and Mirabel, torn between protecting her and protecting the record, secretly copies the ledger's most dangerous pages. The beat is the price of survival becoming personal.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, deep flashback. The chapter traces the night he abandoned his post to save a wounded man the officers had written off, and how that choice made his invisibility a lifelong sentence. The beat is understanding: he has been finishing this work his whole life without knowing it.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The boatyard burns on the eve of the inquiry—arson ambiguous, possibly Corvane, possibly a frightened resident. Mirabel runs into the smoke for the ledger; Odile pulls him out with only half the book. The beat is devastating loss and the climax's ignition: what survives must now be spoken.

chapters.title: Reading the Names Aloud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the inquiry, Mirabel abandons his safe testimony and reads every surviving name from the charred ledger, implicating Corvane's falsified reports and himself. The beat is the climax: exposure chosen over safety, silence broken at last.

chapters.title: Where the Harbor Breaks
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing with Mirabel. The yard is lost but the inquiry rules the deaths must be recorded; the found family disperses to new harbors, carrying copied pages. Mirabel begins a fresh ledger—not of the erased, but of the living. The beat is bittersweet resolution: the work continues, no longer in hiding.
